hooks.name: documentation-sync
hooks.description: After a spec task completes, update docs/kiro_build_log.md (and README.md only on material user-facing change) from the observed code changes and test results. Documentation-only: no source edits, no simulations, no commits.

action.prompt:
A spec task has just completed. Sync the project documentation with what actually happened. This is a documentation-only step.

1. Gather evidence (read-only):
   - Identify the completed task: its spec directory under .kiro/specs/ and its task ID and text in tasks.md.
   - Inspect the real changes with cheap read-only commands, e.g. `git status --short`, `git diff --stat`, `git diff`, `git log --oneline -5`. Read changed files as needed.
   - Collect test and command results that were actually observed during this task (in this session's tool output or in saved artifacts such as docs/milestones/*.md or runs/ manifests). Do not run tests, rollouts, searches, simulations, network calls or builds to produce new numbers.

2. Update docs/kiro_build_log.md:
   - Preserve its existing structure: one `## <Milestone> — <title>` section per milestone, a short spec/branch/tag paragraph, then a table `| Task | Kiro spec output | Commit | Observed verification |`.
   - Add or extend the row for the completed task in the current milestone's section. Create a new milestone section only if none exists yet, following the same format.
   - Record: what was implemented; important architectural decisions (link an ADR in docs/decision-log/ if one exists); problems encountered and how they were solved; test results actually observed (exact command, pass/fail counts, timings as reported); remaining limitations.
   - Keep rows concise. Put longer decision/problem/limitation notes in a short paragraph or bullets under that milestone's table, matching existing entries.
   - If the commit is not yet made, write `uncommitted` instead of a hash. If no tests were observed for this task, write `tests not run in this task`.

3. Update README.md only if this task materially changed user-facing functionality, setup steps, CLI commands, dependencies, or application behavior. Edit the relevant existing section (Setup, Test, Run, Documentation) in place; do not restructure the file. Otherwise leave README.md untouched.

4. Accuracy rules:
   - Never invent results, benchmarks, metrics, commit hashes or completed features. Every number must come from observed output or a saved artifact.
   - Distinguish implemented and verified work from planned work. Planned work is not listed in the build log until it has been run (the log's own rule).
   - Do not describe the CPU adapter as PPO or fine-tuning, and do not claim a policy improved unless the validation gate actually passed.

5. Avoid churn:
   - Before writing, check whether the task is already documented. Update the existing entry instead of adding a duplicate.
   - If nothing material changed (for example a docs-only or no-op task), make no edits and say so.

6. Constraints:
   - Edit only docs/kiro_build_log.md and, when warranted, README.md.
   - Do not modify source code, tests, specs, steering files, hooks, or milestone reports.
   - Do not run expensive commands and do not stage or commit anything.

Finish with a two-line note: which files changed (or 'no documentation changes'), and the evidence each change is based on.
